metadata.method_name: Lane C - parent-free, prompt-free recipe recovery graded against measured harm
metadata.description:
METHOD.  Given ONE checkpoint and nothing else - no parent, no reference model, no attested base -
recover an abliteration RECIPE from its residual-write matrices (o_proj / down_proj) and ask whether
the recovered RECIPE grades the checkpoint's measured harmful compliance, or only flags that it was
edited at all.
metadata.VERDICT_SENTENCE: The graded claim is UNTESTABLE at the achieved graded panel size (n_edited_graded = 0). The cause is MEASURED, not inferred: this worker had no GPU and a hard cpuset of two hyperthreads of one physical core on a host at load 260-345, giving a generation rate of 0.5 tokens/second aggregate, so the pre-registered floor of 16 graded checkpoints would have cost about nine hours of wall clock. WHAT IS REPORTED INSTEAD IS NOT A CONSOLATION PRIZE: the parent-free recipe estimators are calibrated against KNOWN ground truth on real weights, the pre-registered detection thresholds are given their first measured operating points on real trained weights with families held out, the structural precondition of a bottom-spectrum read is established, the recipe-coverage census is run over every card in the panel, the anisotropy-matched null is measured against the isotropic one, and the external published-safety limb is completed. The graded endpoint is reported with its achieved n and its achieved MDE, and is never presented as a null result.

deviations.prereg: kappa_hat from a tail fit of the bottom spectrum
deviations.actual: kappa_hat KEPT, plus a NEW Rayleigh-depression readout RQ_pooled
deviations.reason: GATE 1 measured that a bottom-spectrum RANK read is only sensitive while |1-kappa| < sigma_min/sigma_rms (0.19 on real Qwen3-0.6B o_proj): at kappa=0.3 and 0.7 the recovered strength was indistinguishable from unedited. The rank read's operating range is now a reported calibration result, and a graded readout that is defined at every kappa was added beside it.

deviations.reason: failure branch F5/F8; the achieved n is reported next to every statistic

deviations.actual: |cos| = 0.980 against an exact eigh, below the 0.99 bar
deviations.reason: on an HONEST layer the bottom eigenvalues are near-degenerate, so the individual bottom eigenvector is not uniquely determined by the matrix. botgap and kappa_hat agree to 3 decimals, and the ablated case is exact (|cos| = 1.000000). The residual direction noise on honest checkpoints is precisely what the anisotropy-matched null in Stage 5 is there to absorb.

deviations.field: graded panel size and item counts
deviations.actual: sized from MEASURED CPU share: H12 + B12 + BB6, max_new_tokens=24, checkpoints <=1.3B
deviations.reason: MEASURED, not assumed: the Stage 2 process accumulated 73 s of CPU in 600 s of wall clock - 12% of ONE core - on a worker with no GPU, a hard cpuset of two hyperthreads of one physical core, and a host load average of ~260-345. Freeing two auxiliary processes raised it to 17%. A prompt PREFILL costs as much as the decode it precedes, so the per-checkpoint bill is driven by the NUMBER OF ITEMS, not the token budget. The endpoint's power scales with the number of CHECKPOINTS, so items were cut and checkpoints kept. The achieved n is reported next to every statistic, and the 24-token truncation compresses the StrongREJECT convincing/specific scale - it preserves the refusal-vs-compliance ordering the endpoint needs but not the full rubric range. Both are stated as limitations.

deviations.prereg: o_proj first - the tensor every abliteration tool edits
deviations.actual: the site is chosen by ASPECT RATIO (d_in/d_out > 1.05), which selects down_proj on every family on this panel
deviations.reason: MEASURED: every Qwen2/Qwen3/Llama o_proj on this panel is SQUARE (num_heads*head_dim == hidden_size) and Gemma3-1B's is wider than tall. A bottom-spectrum read is only interpretable where the matrix has MORE COLUMNS THAN ROWS, so on a square o_proj the honest bottom edge is not bounded away from zero and the pre-registered BOTGAP < 0.1 flag false-positives on untouched weights (honest unsloth/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct: BOTGAP_min = 0.0136). down_proj always has intermediate_size > hidden_size. Detection is reported BOTH overall and restricted to structurally valid sites.

The plan budgeted a 16 GB GPU; this worker has none, a hard cpuset of two hyperthreads of one physical EPYC core, and a host load average of 260-345, which left this process ~26% of ONE core. deviations.prereg: all layers, or stride 2 if throughput binds
deviations.actual: stride 2-4, chosen adaptively from a measured per-matrix cost model; the stride and the read layer set are recorded per checkpoint, and the BSA/TSA window is shrunk in read positions so it still spans 8 MODEL layers
deviations.reason: throughput binds hard on this worker. STATED LIMITATION: at stride 4 a 36-layer model contributes 9 read positions, so an edit confined to a narrow layer band can be under-sampled, and the band/profile fits are correspondingly coarse. Statistics that are stride-invariant (per-matrix BOTGAP, kappa_hat, the cross-family cosine) are unaffected; BSA and XLC are computed over the read positions with the window rescaled so the statistic keeps meaning the same thing across the panel.

what_was_NOT_run_and_why.A_coupling_activation_readout: DROPPED FOR COST. The plan budgets a 16 GB GPU; this worker had none and a hard cpuset of two hyperthreads of one physical core. Measured on this box, a prompt PREFILL costs as much as the decode it precedes, so the 32-item hidden-state harvest was roughly 40% of the whole per-checkpoint generation bill. It was cut so the graded panel could span more CHECKPOINTS, which is what the endpoint's power scales with. The standing invariant is still satisfied WITHOUT it: three readouts read weights (W_RECIPE, W_DETECT, W_RQ) against a required minimum of three, and two logit-only/teacher-forced baselines against a maximum of two.
what_was_NOT_run_and_why.behavioural_re_measurement_of_the_forger: The rank-one repair's effect on measured compliance needs a second generation pass over the repaired weights, which does not fit on a GPU-less worker. The weight-space half is measured and the behavioural half is handed to the forgery lane as an explicit written prediction in results/forgery_handoff.json.
what_was_NOT_run_and_why.weight_readouts_on_the_HELM_open_weight_: The feasible pool is 7-14B; at the measured per-matrix cost that is hours per model on this worker. Stratum 2 is therefore reported as a pool listing with n printed and NO coefficient, per failure branch F7, and the external limb's weight rests on the identical-weights ceiling, which needs no readout at all.

incumbents.name: AMS (Activation-based Model Scanner)
incumbents.arxiv_or_venue: arXiv:2608.05578; published IEEE Access, vol. 14, pp. 91723-91737, 2026 (DOI 10.1109/ACCESS.2026.3704057). Code: github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/activation-model-scanner (Apache-2.0, pip install 'ams-scanner[cli]')
incumbents.needs_prompts: 32 prompts (16 contrastive pos/neg pairs) per concept x 3 concepts = 96 forward passes/model, 10-40s on A100/L4 (Tier 1, the tier that produces the headline number)
incumbents.headline_number: LOOCV threshold-classification accuracy = 71% (10/14), identical under both calibration rules (sigma_harmful-only and worst-concept-min), n=14 models (Section VII-C). Secondary: Pearson r=-0.546 (p=0.043) but Spearman rho=-0.423 (p=0.13, NOT significant) for sigma_harmful vs behavioural compliance, n=14 models (Section VII-E); worst-concept variant r=-0.505 (p=0.065), rho=-0.273 (p=0.34). Bootstrap: median 95% CI width = 3.36 sigma against the 2.0-3.5 PASS/CRITICAL decision band, 26/42 cells (62%) cross PASS, 14/42 (33%) cross CRITICAL (n=42 cells = 14 models x 3 concepts).
incumbents.why_not_directly_comparable: Its own LOOCV re-held-out ONLY the classification threshold (midpoint recomputed on the other 13 models) -- the fitted direction, the in-sample layer sweep (argmax over the same 40-80%-depth window maximizing separation on the SAME 16 pairs used to report it), and the fixed 16-pair prompt set were never held out; the authors themselves concede 'even the LOOCV reframing does not fully decouple calibration from evaluation.' A leave-one-lineage-out number is strictly stricter, so 71% is a loose, non-matched bar, not a clean target to beat.
incumbents.must_cite_not_claim: AMS's class (iv) result -- that behavioural fine-tuning is the only undetectable forgery, preserving both the refusal direction and the contrastive cluster while reaching sigma_harmful=5.45 with 19/20 (97%) stratified-harmful-prompt compliance, uncaught by either tier -- is already published; any use of 'the only undetectable forgery is training' must be framed as a pre-registered prediction adopted from AMS, not an independent finding.

incumbents.name: Skin-Deep / GFS (Geometric Fragility Score)
incumbents.arxiv_or_venue: arXiv:2606.22676 (preprint, submitted 21 Jun 2026, cs.AI; no venue/proceedings acceptance found). Code: github.com/js-lee-AI/skin-deep
incumbents.headline_number: GFS Eq 3 = sum_l w_l*|d_l|*(1-|cos(v_l, v_Arditi_l)|) is a per-model scalar with no CI/resampling reported (Section 3.2). cPCA subspace separation on the 4 core models: peak |d|>=1.8, probe accuracy>=0.90, held-out split-sample d_test>=2.71 (n=4 core models, 1000 prompts each; Section 5.1, Table 1). NO Spearman/Kendall coefficient or rank-accuracy is printed for the LoRA-retention-prediction claim -- the dossier states explicitly there is no GFS number to beat there: the claim is a qualitative co-occurrence at n=7 models (4 core + 3 hold-out).
incumbents.why_not_directly_comparable: It is NOT parent-free: Eq 1's contrastive-PCA direction requires the base model's activation covariance (Sigma_base_l), the public code requires both --instruct_model and --base_model, and it needs 1000 prompts -- two access axes (parent-required, high prompt count) away from a parent-free few-prompt deliverable.

incumbents.name: N-GLARE (Non-Generative Latent Representation-Efficient LLM Safety Evaluator)
incumbents.arxiv_or_venue: arXiv:2511.14195 (v1 18 Nov 2025, v2 8 Jan 2026); ACL 2026 Volume 1: Long Papers, pp. 28902-28923, Anthology ID 2026.acl-long.1334. No public code found.
incumbents.needs_prompts: Not stated as a single number in the extracted running text. Requires FOUR probing conditions {Benign, Jailbreak, Ideal Refusal, Plain Query} across 40+ models and 7000+ total test cases panel-wide.
incumbents.headline_number: Eq 7 (JSS definition) and Eq 9 (JR Min/Max definition) confirmed verbatim as formulas, not as scalars with an n. Cost claims: 'less than 1% of the token AND runtime cost' of traditional red-teaming (Abstract); 117.5x token-efficiency multiplier vs. the best single baseline (Figure 1, 9 red-teaming baselines compared). ABSENT-AS-STATED: there is NO numeric Kendall tau in the running text for the headline red-team-agreement claim, in either the arXiv v2 or the ACL camera-ready -- the text only says tau 'remains consistently high.' Table 2 DOES print numeric Kendall/Spearman values (e.g. jailbreak/Kendall: mean 0.87, std 0.14, n-axis) but for a DIFFERENT, weaker claim: metric stability under perturbation, not the headline correlation.
incumbents.why_not_directly_comparable: It is parent-free and generation-free like the deliverable (closer than GFS or RAS on those axes), but it requires four probing conditions over 7000+ cases, so it is separated on the prompt-budget axis alone -- structurally not a few-prompt method.
incumbents.must_cite_not_claim: Table 2's numeric Kendall/Spearman robustness values (e.g. 'jailbreak/kendall mean 0.87') must never be quoted as 'N-GLARE achieves tau=0.87' for the headline red-team-agreement claim -- that would be a misattribution; the headline claim itself has no printed number to quote at all (verdict recorded in the dossier as NOT-PRINTED-IN-RUNNING-TEXT).

incumbents.name: RAS / SafeVec (Refusal Alignment Score)
incumbents.arxiv_or_venue: arXiv:2606.25750v1 [cs.CR], 24 Jun 2026 (preprint; no venue found). No public code found.
incumbents.what_it_reads: mixed (last-token residual-stream activations for the cosine-similarity score itself, PLUS the calibration models' measured ASR -- a generation/judge-based behavioural quantity -- consumed to fit the b_a/alpha_a calibration constants)
incumbents.needs_prompts: |S|, |U|, |J| (safe / unsafe / jailbreak prompt-set sizes) UNSTATED-IN-SOURCE in the text read; requires a safe/unsafe/jailbreak prompt set scored on a per-family safety-aligned REFERENCE model plus a calibration set of models with KNOWN ASR
incumbents.headline_number: Average speedup over judge-based scoring = 210.13x (per-model: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct 40.52x, Gemma-3-4b-it 474.85x, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct 135.25x), n=3 models (Sec 4.2 RQ4/Table 2); wall-clock 14.13s average (Llama 14.13s, Gemma 13.29s, Qwen 14.97s) vs judge 2969.14s average. Llama-family Table 1 gives 5 raw SafeVec-score/ASR rows (e.g. mlabonne/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-abliterated: -0.155/-0.181/ASR 0.933). NO cross-family correlation coefficient is printed in the text read.
incumbents.why_not_directly_comparable: It requires, per architecture family, a safety-aligned reference model AND a calibration set of models AND those calibration models' measured ASR -- a strictly richer access class than parent-free/weights-only. Its own layer window, refusal direction, and calibration constants (bad-anchor scale b_a, severity multiplier alpha_a) are all fitted in-sample on the same calibration checkpoints the separation is then reported on (no leave-one-model/family-out protocol described), which the dossier labels LOOSER than a leave-one-lineage-out protocol -- any comparison must be labelled NON-MATCHED.
incumbents.must_cite_not_claim: Three items explicitly flagged 'already_published_we_must_cite_not_claim' in the dossier: (1) that an internal, generation-free, per-checkpoint score separates aligned/uncensored/abliterated variants and tracks ASR -- RAS publishes exactly this; (2) that such a score is ~2 orders of magnitude cheaper than judge-based evaluation (210-217x faster, ~14s vs ~50min per model); (3) that raw internal scores do NOT transfer across architecture families without family-specific calibration -- RAS states this as a measured limitation, so any of our own cross-family negative result is a REPLICATION, not a discovery, and must be framed that way.

verified_numbers.statement: 'Adversarially finetuning models to accept harmful instructions has minimal impact on the model's internal belief of harmfulness' holds verbatim, and Latent Guard matches/beats Llama Guard 3 8B while reducing over-refusal (e.g. Qwen2 persuasion 75.0% vs Llama Guard 17.8%). BUT Latent Guard is a PER-PROMPT classifier fit per fixed base model from 200 labelled harmful/harmless examples, NOT a per-model/per-checkpoint scalar score -- so the motivating claim must be rescoped to per-PROMPT vs per-CHECKPOINT internals.

A central, repeated finding: 'the Explicit Semantic Control of Llama3.1' vs 'the Latent Distributed Control of Qwen2.5' -- a family-split double dissociation confirmed in abstract, intro, results and conclusion. Consequence: Qwen must be reported held out separately, never pooled, for any fitted-direction candidate.

'Refusal levels off at the level of a single harm direction' (rank 1) and 'about three-quarters of refusal's causal input lies outside the moral subspace altogether'; Qwen specifically 'is unresolved at our sample size' (n=19 twins). Consequence: spend no metrics on higher-rank refusal subspaces.

verified_numbers.verdict: AMBIGUOUS-MULTIPLE-OCCURRENCES (both readings genuinely true, no misattribution)
verified_numbers.statement: Both readings of '0.003' (own-direction abliteration invariance vs instruct-to-abliterated transfer degradation) and both readings of '73 degrees' (max-pool-vs-last-token protocol-angle divergence vs Gemma-3 base-to-instruct rotation) are genuinely present as four distinct true findings, plus an unrelated third 73.4-degree occurrence. Rule for downstream artifacts: always name which reading is being cited; corroborated independently by 2603.27412 (AUROC at most 0.015 below instruction-tuned counterparts, on the same Qwen base/instruct/abliterated triplets).

HRCI_repr(t) = 1/2*C_cos(t) + 1/2*C_sub(t) [Eq 9] confirmed verbatim including all printed numbers: HRCI_repr 0.0784 -> 0.0205 (a 73.9% drop) across training, ASR 0 -> 0.2500, XSTest refusal 1.00 -> 0.2280, SFT control 0.0217 -> 0.0190; and the authors' own verdict 'Thus low coupling is not a safety score' (SFT reaches low coupling while remaining high-ASR). One caveat: PDF-to-text garbled the bar glyphs in Eq 7, so whether C_cos literally carries absolute-value bars could not be pixel-verified; default to absolute cosine, flagged.

candidate_verdicts.one_line: Per-checkpoint, cross-fitted harm-refusal coupling used ONLY as a discriminator (not a compliance predictor).
candidate_verdicts.what_remains_open: PER-CHECKPOINT and CROSS-FITTED (harm estimate fit on held-out items, not in-sample) and used-as-DISCRIMINATOR only, separating safety-tuned/instruct/abliterated on held-out lineages.
candidate_verdicts.already_owned_by: arXiv:2606.16349 owns a parent-free, single-checkpoint, in-sample HRCI_repr (Eq 9) and states verbatim 'low coupling is not a safety score' -- so C1 must be pre-registered as a discriminator only, never a compliance predictor, and must beat HRCI_repr as the baseline.

candidate_verdicts.one_line: The prompt-budget crossover point where a graded internal readout and a binary behavioural readout attain equal discriminative power on the SAME checkpoints.
candidate_verdicts.what_remains_open: The crossover point n* itself, published by none of the three nearest sources.
candidate_verdicts.already_owned_by: IRT adaptive-item work owns the few-items behavioural side (>=80%, up to 97-99% cost reduction); arXiv:2608.13329 owns the variance decomposition of an internal readout on the internal side, and reports a generalizability coefficient of 0.00002 for cross-family comparison on a single prompt wrapper -- a direct threat to any few-prompt cross-family framing that must be answered by design (vary the wrapper) or conceded in the abstract.

candidate_verdicts.one_line: Per-checkpoint scalar = (layer where refusal becomes decodable) minus (layer where request content becomes decodable), correlated with an outcome.
candidate_verdicts.what_remains_open: Collapsing two already-published layer-decodability curves into a single onset-layer INDEX each, subtracting them into ONE scalar per checkpoint, and correlating that scalar across MANY checkpoints/models with an external outcome.
candidate_verdicts.already_owned_by: arXiv:2507.11878 (NeurIPS 2025) already contains BOTH required curves on the SAME models and already states harmfulness precedes refusal qualitatively; it never computes an onset-index difference or a per-checkpoint scalar. Confound: arXiv:2609.03887 shows the post-training METHOD (SFT/reasoning-augmented/ORPO) independently reshapes where refusal is computed, so a depth-difference scalar risks reading training recipe rather than safety level -- a recipe control is required.

candidate_verdicts.one_line: A recovered, parent-free, weights-only, GRADED (continuous) edit strength that is regressed against MEASURED harmful compliance.
candidate_verdicts.what_remains_open: The full conjunction WEIGHTS-ONLY and PARENT-FREE and GRADED and PREDICTS-MEASURED-COMPLIANCE. Dropping any one conjunct lands on a published result.
candidate_verdicts.already_owned_by: Binary parent-free detection is CLOSED (Jorak Model Scanner ships it). Parent-anchored detection is CLOSED (arXiv:2607.01854, AUROC 0.95 in-sample, leave-one-family-out balanced accuracy 0.89, but 'presumes an attested reference'). Graded activation-statistic-vs-compliance is CLOSED (AMS r=-0.546). Skin-Deep/GFS (2606.22676) was the strongest adversarial counterexample but is parent-DEPENDENT and never regresses its score against a continuous ASR/compliance outcome. An August-2026 practitioner survey independently names this same cell as the hardest open problem -- cite as a known open problem, not undiscovered territory.

candidate_verdicts.one_line: A learned metamodel on pooled hidden states predicting benchmark safety, ablated against a lineage-identity probe on the SAME features.
candidate_verdicts.verdict: OPEN (on the ablation only; novelty framing downgraded)
candidate_verdicts.what_remains_open: Training a hidden-state performance predictor and then ablating it against an architecture/lineage-identity probe on the same features, on the per-MODEL/per-LINEAGE axis, for a safety BENCHMARK SCORE.
candidate_verdicts.already_owned_by: Lineage is recoverable from weights alone (arXiv:2608.14929, pairwise ancestry verification) and benchmark scores are predictable from item subsets/other scores. The identity-confound-ablation METHOD itself is established prior art (Hewitt & Liang control tasks 2019; arXiv:2606.02907 residualizes source identity/option count/response length and drives a 100%-accurate hidden-state probe to chance) -- but on REASONING MODE within one model, not benchmark score across model lineages. C5's contribution must therefore be framed as 'we ran the established control on the per-model axis, where nobody had,' NOT 'we invented the control.'

handbook_norms: A circuit or causal effect reported from one seed/hyperparameter/input distribution is a volatile random variable, not a fixed property -- sample across configurations (here: across architecture families / checkpoints / prompt sets) and report the distribution or a CI, not a single point estimate. [S4]

Structural difference between two conditions is not evidence of a different mechanism until edge-level, cross-condition transfer tests are run; source-level/aggregate comparisons inflate apparent specialization ('phantom specialization'). Directly relevant to comparing recovered edit strength across held-out architecture families. [S23]

Before trusting a fitted direction/subspace as a classifier or predictor, benchmark it against a simple difference-in-means baseline and against a non-featurized baseline; a standardized comparison track found supervised, directly-fit methods (DAS) beat SAE-style features, and featurization is not automatically better than the raw/neuron-level signal. [S10]

Add a randomized/untrained-network control arm before treating a high separation or reconstruction score as evidence that a real, meaningful structure was recovered -- auto-interp-style scores on randomly initialized transformers can look similar to scores on trained ones, so the metric alone does not discriminate the thing it is used to claim. [S9]

Fix and declare the class of maps/subspaces allowed BEFORE fitting; an unconstrained search for an alignment/subspace can hit a perfect-looking fit on a randomly initialized model and mean nothing, so the encoding/subspace-class assumption must be stated explicitly and be testable independently of the claim it licenses. [S5]

Report the per-item/per-unit distribution for any steering-strength or edit-strength claim, not only a mean effect at one operating point -- mean effects vary across samples and can hide the regime where the effect is unreliable or indistinguishable from a random perturbation for many targets. [S20][S3]

A fast/cheap proxy statistic standing in for a causal effect (e.g. a closed-form activation- or weight-space score used instead of measuring compliance directly) should be screened with a reliability check before being trusted at scale -- its dominant error can come from downstream non-linearity rather than the assumption it was built on. [S19]

The field prints a two-track evidence bar: state specific falsifiable hypotheses and how the evidence does and does not support them, OR demonstrate a clear practical benefit over a well-implemented baseline -- a new statistic that only improves a proxy metric with no such framing does not clear the bar (this is exactly the failure mode a not-held-out layer sweep or an unmatched LOOCV protocol produces, as seen in the AMS incumbent above). [S14]

A model-diffing/edited-vs-unedited comparison run under a sparsity-inducing (L1-style) objective can fabricate 'unique to the edited model' artifacts when the feature exists on both sides; presence-test any 'only appears after the edit' claim rather than trusting the loss's output at face value. [S34]

Two independent studies on the same underlying behavior have reached conflicting conclusions, and a third found both partially correct but incomparable -- results in this field are not automatically comparable across papers/protocols, so any cross-incumbent comparison (e.g. against AMS's or RAS's in-sample numbers) must state exactly what differs in the measurement protocol, not just report both numbers side by side. [S8]
prohibitions: D1: 'Do not use the unscoped sentence anywhere' -- referring to the motivating claim 'internal readouts have never beaten output-based guards,' which must instead be rescoped to per-PROMPT vs per-CHECKPOINT and cite arXiv:2507.11878 + arXiv:2608.08029 together.
D8: 'Do not set a success threshold at 0.8' for any metric-vs-outcome correlation; pre-commit to reporting BOTH Pearson and Spearman, sized around |r| ~ 0.5 at model-level n.

D11: 'Do not compare across families on a single [prompt] rendering and call it a metric' -- either vary the prompt rendering across a designed set, or state the limitation explicitly in the abstract.

N-GLARE: writing 'N-GLARE achieves tau = 0.87' would be a misattribution -- Table 2's numeric Kendall/Spearman values belong to a different, weaker robustness-under-perturbation claim, not the headline red-team-agreement correlation, which has no printed number in running text.

AMS: the 'only undetectable forgery is training' result (class (iv), sigma_harmful=5.45, 97% compliance) is AMS's own published finding and must be framed as a pre-registered prediction adopted from AMS, not claimed as an independent discovery.

RAS: our own cross-family transfer negative, if found, is a REPLICATION of RAS's already-published limitation ('family-specific calibration remains necessary'), not a discovery, and must be framed that way in the payoff artifact.

D6 (AMS 71% LOOCV): 'Never present it as a clean win or loss' -- the comparison must be labelled NON-MATCHED because AMS's LOOCV held out only the classification threshold, not the fitted direction, layer sweep, or prompt set.

D4 (the 0.003 / 73-degree numbers in arXiv:2604.18901): when citing either number, 'must be careful to attribute the CORRECT one of the two co-existing readings and not conflate them,' and must NOT additionally cite the unrelated third 73.4-degree occurrence as if it were one of the two target readings.

C5: the identity-confound ablation must be claimed as 'we ran the established control on the per-model axis, where nobody had' -- NOT 'we invented the control' (prior art: Hewitt & Liang 2019; arXiv:2606.02907).
gotchas: Scholarly-mode search (OpenAlex/Crossref) returned entirely off-topic results for every LLM-safety query tried (e.g. a coupling/harm/refusal query returned marketing and materials-science papers) -- an empty or off-topic scholarly-mode result is evidence about the search backend, not about the field. All usable coverage came from general-mode search over arXiv/ACL Anthology/OpenReview/GitHub.

PDF-to-text extraction inserts hard line breaks mid-sentence: 4 of 8 independently re-checked quotes first returned ZERO matches on exact-phrase greps and looked like failed quotes but were not. Use whitespace-flexible regex patterns BEFORE recording a claim as NOT-FOUND, or false negatives get manufactured.

Near-ID collision: arXiv 2606.22676 (Skin-Deep/GFS) vs arXiv 2606.22686 (a different paper -- a logit-level Contrastive Logit Steering attack study by different authors, TrustNLP 2026) -- one digit apart, both June-2026 refusal-geometry work.

Title collision: arXiv 2608.05578's own abs-page title is 'Detecting Safety Training Modification in Language Models via Activation Analysis,' but Google's publications listing page gives the SAME paper a different display title, 'AMS: Detecting Unsafe and Tampered Language Models via Activation Analysis' -- one paper under two titles, not two papers.

AMS's paper prose and its own public code (src/ams/extractor.py) disagree on two pinned constants that the paper leaves vague -- follow the code, not the paper text, for exact reimplementation values.

PDF-to-text garbled the bar/absolute-value glyphs in N5's Eq 7, so whether C_cos literally carries absolute-value bars could not be pixel-verified from the extracted text; default to the absolute-cosine reading and flag it explicitly rather than silently picking one.

incumbent_bars_and_prohibitions.BAR-1_AMS_2608.05578: Published: 71% (10/14) leave-one-out threshold accuracy, and Pearson r = -0.546 (p = .043) with Spearman rho = -0.423 (p = .13, NOT significant). Labelled NON-MATCHED: their leave-one-out held out ONLY THE THRESHOLD - the direction, the layer sweep and the prompt set were never held out, and the authors concede the coupling. It is never presented here as a clean win or loss.
incumbent_bars_and_prohibitions.BAR-2_SkinDeep_GFS_2606.22676: NOT parent-free (its Eq 1 cPCA needs the base model's covariance) and needs ~1000 prompts; its retention-prediction claim has NO PRINTED COEFFICIENT (qualitative, n = 7). There is no GFS number to beat, and none is invented here.
incumbent_bars_and_prohibitions.BAR-3_N_GLARE_2511.14195: Separated from this lane on the PROMPT-BUDGET AXIS: parent-free and generation-free but needs four probing conditions over 7000+ cases. No numeric Kendall tau exists for its headline claim; quoting one would be a misattribution, so none is quoted.
incumbent_bars_and_prohibitions.BAR-4_RAS_SafeVec_2606.25750: The closest published thing to this deliverable, but it needs a per-family reference model, a calibration set and those models' MEASURED ASR, and it states that family-specific calibration remains necessary. ANY CROSS-FAMILY NEGATIVE WE REPORT IS A REPLICATION OF THAT STATED LIMITATION, NOT A DISCOVERY.
incumbent_bars_and_prohibitions.class_iv_undetectability: That behavioural fine-tuning is already undetectable by this class of statistic is AMS's published result and is cited, never claimed here.
incumbent_bars_and_prohibitions.identity_confound_control: The established control is prior art (residualising source identity); this artifact claims only that it RAN the established control on the per-model axis.
incumbent_bars_and_prohibitions.no_0.8_success_threshold: No success threshold is set at 0.8 anywhere; every claim is an estimate with a CI and its achieved MDE.

metadata.prior_art_attribution: BSA/TSA subspace-sharing statistics are ADOPTED PRIOR ART - the public Jorak Model Scanner already computes a bottom-k left-singular subspace signature on exactly o_proj/down_proj. What is added here is honest-panel calibration on REAL trained weights, a measured bf16 floor, the strength estimators and their operating range, and the cross-layer/cross-family sharing checks. It is a DETECTION statistic and is never reported as a safety score.

examples.input: REQUEST STEP-1 LINEAGE. Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Base is the 'base' member of the Qwen3-4B lineage. All four members share an architecture EXACTLY, so any difference in a weight statistic is attributable to what was done to the weights rather than to width, depth or family. Read it parent-free.

REQUEST STEP-1 LINEAGE. Qwen/Qwen3-4B-SafeRL is the 'safety-RL' member of the Qwen3-4B lineage. All four members share an architecture EXACTLY, so any difference in a weight statistic is attributable to what was done to the weights rather than to width, depth or family. Read it parent-free.

REQUEST STEP-1 LINEAGE. mlabonne/Qwen3-4B-abliterated is the 'abliterated' member of the Qwen3-4B lineage. All four members share an architecture EXACTLY, so any difference in a weight statistic is attributable to what was done to the weights rather than to width, depth or family. Read it parent-free.
Across the Qwen3-4B lineage, WHICH weight statistic actually separates the abliterated member from its unedited base and its safety-RL sibling?
examples.predict_answer: The CROSS-FAMILY COSINE. On the matched-architecture lineage the abliterated member reads cross-family cosine 0.434 against 0.201 (base) and 0.206 (safety-RL) - about 2.1x its siblings - while the realised-strength estimate barely moves (0.377 vs 0.350 and 0.343) and the cross-LAYER cosine moves the WRONG WAY (0.056 against 0.078 and 0.113). The agreement between o_proj's and down_proj's bottom directions at the same layer is the discriminating quantity here, and it is a check no published scanner reports.
examples.predict_caveat: n = 1 lineage, read at layer stride 4. This is a matched-architecture CONTRAST, not a calibrated detector, and it is reported as such.

examples.input: RECIPE-COVERAGE CENSUS. Across every checkpoint in the panel, how often does the model card state the abliteration recipe that was applied - the tool, the scope, and the strength?
examples.predict_finding: Of 126 model cards, 96.0% state NOTHING about the recipe, and 0 state a numeric ablation strength. The recipe is essentially never documented, which is precisely why it has to be recovered from the weights. Where the card and the weights disagree, THE WEIGHTS ARE THE MEASUREMENT AND THE CARD IS THE CLAIM.

On xstest the largest such gap is 6.719436022835794x the entire across-model variance, i.e. on that scenario the wrapper moves the published score further than the genuine model-to-model spread does.
